operations\">Reactive context and async operations\u003C\u002Fa>\n  \u003C\u002Fh3>\n  \u003Cp>The reactive context is only active for synchronous code. Any signal reads that occur after an asynchronous boundary will not be tracked as dependencies.\u003C\u002Fp>\n\u003Cdiv class=\"docs-code docs-code-avoid\">\n    \u003Cdiv class=\"docs-code-header\">\u003Cspan class=\"docs-code-header-style \">Avoid\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fdiv>\n    \u003Cpre class=\"shiki shiki-themes github-light github-dark\" style=\"--shiki-light:#24292e;--shiki-dark:#e1e4e8;--shiki-light-bg:#fff;--shiki-dark-bg:#24292e\" tabindex=\"0\">\u003Ccode>\u003Cspan class=\"line\">\u003Ca style=\"--shiki-light:#6F42C1;--shiki-dark:#B392F0\" href=\"\u002Fapi\u002Fcore\u002Feffect\">effect\u003C\u002Fa>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\">(\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583\">async\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\"> () \u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583\">=&gt;\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\"> {\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fspan>\n\u003Cspan class=\"line\">\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583\">  const\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF\"> data\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583\"> =\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583\"> await\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#6F42C1;--shiki-dark:#B392F0\"> fetchUserData\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\">();\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fspan>\n\u003Cspan class=\"line\">\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#6A737D;--shiki-dark:#6A737D\">  \u002F\u002F Reactive context is lost here - theme() won't be tracked\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fspan>\n\u003Cspan class=\"line\">\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\">  console.\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#6F42C1;--shiki-dark:#B392F0\">log\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\">(\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF\">`User: ${\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\">data\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF\">.\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\">name\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF\">}, Theme: ${\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#6F42C1;--shiki-dark:#B392F0\">theme\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF\">()\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF\">}`\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\">);\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fspan>\n\u003Cspan class=\"line\">\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\">});\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fcode>\u003C\u002Fpre>\n  \u003C\u002Fdiv>\u003Cp>To ensure all signal reads are tracked, read signals before the \u003Ccode>await\u003C\u002Fcode>. This includes passing them as arguments to the awaited function, since arguments are evaluated synchronously:\u003C\u002Fp>\n\u003Cdiv class=\"docs-code docs-code-prefer\">\n    \u003Cdiv \u003Cdiv class=\"docs-code-header\">\u003Cspan class=\"docs-code-header-style \">Prefer\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fdiv>\n    \u003Cpre class=\"shiki shiki-themes github-light github-dark\" style=\"--shiki-light:#24292e;--shiki-dark:#e1e4e8;--shiki-light-bg:#fff;--shiki-dark-bg:#24292e\" tabindex=\"0\">\u003Ccode>\u003Cspan class=\"line\">\u003Ca style=\"--shiki-light:#6F42C1;--shiki-dark:#B392F0\" href=\"\u002Fapi\u002Fcore\u002Feffect\">effect\u003C\u002Fa>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\">(\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583\">async\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\"> () \u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583\">=&gt;\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\"> {\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fspan>\n\u003Cspan class=\"line\">\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#6A737D;--shiki-dark:#6A737D\">  \u002F\u002F Also works: signal is read before await (as function argument)\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fspan>\n\u003Cspan class=\"line\">\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583\">  await\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#6F42C1;--shiki-dark:#B392F0\"> renderContent\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\">(\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#6F42C1;--shiki-dark:#B392F0\">docContent\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\">());\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fspan>\n\u003Cspan class=\"line\">\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\">});\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fcode>\u003C\u002Fpre>\n  \u003C\u002Fdiv>\n  \u003Ch2 id=\"advanced-derivations\">\n    \u003Ca href=\"#advanced-derivations\" class=\"docs-anchor\" tabindex=\"-1\" aria-label=\"Link to Advanced derivations\">Advanced derivations\u003C\u002Fa>\n  \u003C\u002Fh2>\n  \u003Cp>While \u003Ca href=\"\u002Fapi\u002Fcore\u002Fcomputed\">\u003Ccode>computed\u003C\u002Fcode>\u003C\u002Fa> handles simple readonly derivations, you might find yourself needing a writable state that is dependent on other signals.\nFor more information see the \u003Ca href=\"\u002Fguide\u002Fsignals\u002Flinked-signal\">Dependent state with linkedSignal\u003C\u002Fa> guide.\u003C\u002Fp>\n\u003Cp>All signal APIs are synchronous— \u003Ca href=\"\u002Fapi\u002Fcore\u002Fsignal\">\u003Ccode>signal\u003C\u002Fcode>\u003C\u002Fa>, \u003Ca href=\"\u002Fapi\u002Fcore\u002Fcomputed\">\u003Ccode>computed\u003C\u002Fcode>\u003C\u002Fa>, \u003Ccode>input\u003C\u002Fcode>, etc. However, applications often need to deal with data that is available asynchronously. A \u003Ca href=\"\u002Fapi\u002Fcore\u002FResource\">\u003Ccode>Resource\u003C\u002Fcode>\u003C\u002Fa> gives you a way to incorporate async data into your application's signal-based code and still allow you to access its data synchronously. For more information see the \u003Ca href=\"\u002Fguide\u002Fsignals\u002Fresource\">Async reactivity with resources\u003C\u002Fa> guide.\u003C\u002Fp>\n\n  \u003Ch2 id=\"executing-side-effects-on-non-reactive-apis\">\n    \u003Ca href=\"#executing-side-effects-on-non-reactive-apis\" class=\"docs-anchor\" tabindex=\"-1\" aria-label=\"Link to Executing side effects on non-reactive APIs\">Executing side effects on non-reactive APIs\u003C\u002Fa>\n  \u003C\u002Fh2>\n  \u003Cp>Synchronous or asynchronous derivations are recommended when we want to react to state changes. However, this doesn't cover all the possible use cases, and you'll sometimes find yourself in a situation where you need to react to signal changes on non-reactive APIs. Use \u003Ca href=\"\u002Fapi\u002Fcore\u002Feffect\">\u003Ccode>effect\u003C\u002Fcode>\u003C\u002Fa> or \u003Ca href=\"\u002Fapi\u002Fcore\u002FafterRenderEffect\">\u003Ccode>afterRenderEffect\u003C\u002Fcode>\u003C\u002Fa> for those specific use cases. For more information see \u003Ca href=\"\u002Fguide\u002Fsignals\u002Feffect\">Side effects for non-reactive APIs\u003C\u002Fa> guide.\u003C\u002Fp>\n\n  \u003Ch2 id=\"reading-signals-in-onpush-components\">\n    \u003Ca href=\"#reading-signals-in-onpush-components\" class=\"docs-anchor\" tabindex=\"-1\" aria-label=\"Link to Reading signals in OnPush components\">Reading signals in \u003Ccode>OnPush\u003C\u002Fcode> components\u003C\u002Fa>\n  \u003C\u002Fh2>\n  \u003Cp>When you read a signal within an \u003Ccode>OnPush\u003C\u002Fcode> component's template, Angular tracks the signal as a dependency of that component. When the value of that signal changes, Angular automatically \u003Ca href=\"api\u002Fcore\u002FChangeDetectorRef#markForCheck\">marks\u003C\u002Fa> the component to ensure it gets updated the next time change detection runs. Refer to the \u003Ca href=\"best-practices\u002Fskipping-subtrees\">Skipping component subtrees\u003C\u002Fa> guide for more information about \u003Ccode>OnPush\u003C\u002Fcode> components.\u003C\u002Fp>\n\n  \u003Ch2 id=\"advanced-topics\">\n    \u003Ca href=\"#advanced-topics\" class=\"docs-anchor\" tabindex=\"-1\" aria-label=\"Link to Advanced topics\">Advanced topics\u003C\u002Fa>\n  \u003C\u002Fh2>\n  \n  \u003Ch3 id=\"signal-equality-functions\">\n    \u003Ca href=\"#signal-equality-functions\" class=\"docs-anchor\" tabindex=\"-1\" aria-label=\"Link to Signal equality functions\">Signal equality functions\u003C\u002Fa>\n  \u003C\u002Fh3>\n  \u003Cp>When creating a signal, you can optionally provide an equality function, which will be used to check whether the new value is actually different than the previous one.\u003C\u002Fp>\n\u003Cdiv class=\"docs-code\">\n    \n    \u003Cpre class=\"shiki shiki-themes github-light github-dark\" style=\"--shiki-light:#24292e;--shiki-dark:#e1e4e8;--shiki-light-bg:#fff;--shiki-dark-bg:#24292e\" tabindex=\"0\">\u003Ccode>\u003Cspan class=\"line\">\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583\">import\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\"> isEqual \u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan class=\"line\">\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#6A737D;--shiki-dark:#6A737D\">\u002F\u002F function will consider the values to be equal, and the signal won't\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fspan>\n\u003Cspan class=\"line\">\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#6A737D;--shiki-dark:#6A737D\">\u002F\u002F trigger any updates.\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003C\u002Fspan>\n\u003Cspan class=\"line\">\u003Cspan style=\"--shiki-light:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8\">data.\u003C\u002Fspan>\u003Cspan writable and computed signals.\u003C\u002Fp>\n\n      \u003Cdiv class=\"docs-alert docs-alert-helpful\">\n        \u003Cp>\u003Cstrong>HELPFUL:\u003C\u002Fstrong> By default, signals use referential equality (\u003Ca href=\"https:\u002F\u002Fdeveloper.mozilla.org\u002Fdocs\u002FWeb\u002FJavaScript\u002FReference\u002FGlobal_Objects\u002FObject\u002Fis\" target=\"_blank\">\u003Ccode>Object.is()\u003C\u002Fcode>\u003C\u002Fa> comparison).\u003C\u002Fp>\n      \u003C\u002Fdiv>\n      \n  \u003Ch3 id=\"type-checking-signals\">\n    \u003Ca href=\"#type-checking-signals\" class=\"docs-anchor\" tabindex=\"-1\" aria-label=\"Link to Type checking signals\">Type checking signals\u003C\u002Fa>\n  \u003C\u002Fh3>\n  \u003Cp>You can use \u003Ca
